text:
The animal known for its long neck is the giraffe.

Jim stood in the center of the advanced yoga studio, a man who had clearly misread the room. He was attempting a variation of the "Standing Split," but his body seemed to have received conflicting instructions from his brain. As he wobbled precariously on one leg, his face turned a shade of crimson that rivaled the instructor’s silk scarf.

"Find your center, Jim," the instructor whispered, though her voice trembled with suppressed laughter.

Jim tried to deepen the stretch. He exhaled sharply, a sound that started as a dignified sigh and ended as a high-pitched squeak. Then, nature intervened. A low, resonant rumble echoed through the silent room, followed by a sharp, percussive *toot* that seemed to vibrate the very floorboards.

The class, a group of serene yogis who had spent years mastering the art of silence, broke. One woman snorted into her mat. A man in the back choked on his own breath. Jim, oblivious to the fact that he had just become the most memorable participant in the studio’s history, grunted again, this time in triumph, as if he had finally nailed the pose. He didn't realize that in the world of advanced yoga, he had just achieved a level of chaos that no amount of meditation could ever replicate.
